title: Gmsh MSH format
overview: Gmsh is a mesh generator and MSH interchange format. OneFLOW currently targets ASCII MSH 4.1 first, with MSH 2.2 ASCII compatibility as a secondary format. The adapter must preserve node and element tags, ordering, entity dimensions/tags, physical names and memberships. The catalog explicitly names Physical Groups as a first-class concept: a physical group is a dimension-tagged collection of geometric entities and must remain distinct from solver boundary-condition semantics.
principle: MSH separates geometric entities from physical groups. MSH 4.1 stores nodes and elements in entity blocks; tags are sparse identities, not dense offsets. $MeshFormat declares version and encoding; $PhysicalNames stores dimension-tagged names; $Entities associates entities and physical groups; $Nodes and $Elements store entity blocks. A physical group is not a OneFLOW boundary-condition type. Physical Groups are declared by dimension and physical tag, then associated with geometric entities; the name is metadata and does not itself prescribe a wall, inlet, outlet or symmetry condition.
architecture: MSH parser -> GmshMesh (source tags, entity ownership and physical memberships) -> UnstructuredMeshData (current first-order staging view) -> UnstructuredCgnsZoneWriter -> CGNS Unstructured Zone. The source parser remains independent of the optional Gmsh SDK. MeshSnapshot/Mesh Core is a broader contract and is not yet the production C++ conversion container.

proves: C++ reader materializes supported ASCII MSH 4.1 data and Gmsh conversion uses the shared UnstructuredMeshData and UnstructuredCgnsZoneWriter.
Knowledge distinguishes entity blocks, sparse tags and physical-group semantics.
does_not_prove: Full MSH 4.1 MeshSnapshot export and complete preservation of source entity identity.
Binary MSH and all high-order element families are supported.
Placeholder .cgns output is a legal CGNS file.
